name: Radiogenic 40Ar source-map and transient-source verification
purpose: Verify D10 spatial weighting, independent absolute normalization, decay/release behavior, and transient options.
production_capability: Radiogenic Ar source and surface inventory.
configuration: The maintained Na-only M2 receipt records argon_source_enabled=false, uniform-global geography, continuous time dependence, the 3.8e20 atoms/s Killen (2002) lower bound, and no map; an Ar-enabled executable must explicitly compile SpeciesList=Na,Ar and enable the dedicated RadiogenicArgon source block.
inputs: D10 qualification metadata and processed regional proxy
independent_reference: Map non-negativity/unit-integral invariant and analytical transient time profiles.
units: dimensionless spatial weight, s^-1, particles m^-2, s
frame_time_convention: D10 lunar coordinates transformed explicitly to MOON_ME_DE421; UTC for transients.
procedure: Verify the compiled uniform-global area partition and strict input receipt; hash and inspect D10; retain SKIPPED until a qualified global map, Ar-linked stochastic injection, and transient source production modes can be evaluated.
acceptance_criteria: No negative weights; unit integral within numerical precision; other thresholds frozen with the production model and cited normalization.
expected_pass_result: Ar injection is reproducible, geographically correct, and independently normalized.
artifacts: result.json containing local production-probe output, exact D10 hashes, QA status, and coverage
status_semantics: The nested local kernel may pass, but U21 remains SKIPPED until global geography, linked Ar injection, and transient criteria exist; corruption is ERROR and an evaluated kernel mismatch is FAIL.
skip_reason: The uniform source kernel exists, but D10 is regional and QA-incomplete and the roadmap's K-weighted/transient linked criteria are unavailable.
missing_capability: Qualified global D10 shape, production potassium-map loader, transient Ar source modes, and an Ar-enabled linked stochastic campaign.
